S: The symptoms have gradually worsened over the past week, worse at night and after long periods of standing. Elevating the legs overnight helps somewhat, though the relief does not last. A family member first noticed the change and suggested this visit. No fever and no new medications.
O: Vitals: temperature 36.8 C, pulse 72, respirations 14, blood pressure 118/76, oxygen saturation 99 percent on room air. Both ankles show pitting swelling that improves with elevation; the skin is intact; the calves are soft and non-tender.
A: Ankle swelling from prolonged standing.
P: Elevate the legs above heart level twice daily for thirty minutes. Take walking breaks every hour when standing is required. Return if swelling becomes one-sided, painful, or accompanied by breathlessness.
rationale: Subjective history is present (timeline, modifiers, what helps) but no chief complaint is ever stated — the note opens with 'The symptoms' and never names them. S-01 missing, S-02 present. Overall incomplete.
